chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ishaq ibn Adam, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Fadl ibn Hassan al-Dalani, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, “May I be made your ransom, I was in my salat (prayer), and in the second rak'ah, while I was reciting, I remembered that I had not said the iqamah, so what should I do?”
He عليه السلام said: “Pause at the point of your recitation and say: ‘Qad qamati al-salat, qad qamati al-salat.’”
Then continue with your recitation and your salat (prayer), and your salat has been completed.”

key_terms.أُقِمْ: I did not say the iqamah, meaning the prayer call immediately preceding congregational or individual salat
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ: the rak'ah, a unit of salat (prayer)
key_terms.امْضِ: continue onward, i.e. proceed without restarting
key_terms.تَمَّتْ صَلَاتُكَ: your salat has been completed, meaning it remains valid
key_terms.صَلَاتِي: my salat (prayer), referring to the ritual prayer already in progress
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: the formula of iqamah meaning 'the salat has been established'

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I remember during salat that I forgot the iqamah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets the iqamah and remembers it during salat, specifically in the second rak'ah while reciting. Imam al-Rida عليه السلام instructs the worshipper not to restart the prayer, but to briefly say “Qad qamati al-salat” and then continue, indicating the validity and completion of the prayer.
